english: For $t\in\mathbb{R}$, let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$, and let $\{t\}=t-[t]$. Let $E=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}:\ \{x\}\neq\dfrac14\right\}$, and let $g:E\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by
Let $S$ be the set of all integers that do not belong to the range of $g$. Then the sum of all the elements of $S$ is ______.
hindi: $t\in\mathbb{R}$ के लिए, माना $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है, तथा $\{t\}=t-[t]$ है। माना $E=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}:\ \{x\}\neq\dfrac14\right\}$ है, तथा $g:E\to\mathbb{R}$ निम्न द्वारा परिभाषित है
माना $S$ उन सभी पूर्णांकों का समुच्चय है जो $g$ के परिसर में नहीं हैं। तब $S$ के सभी अवयवों का योग ______ है।
solution: Let $u=\{x\}-\dfrac14$. As $x$ varies over $E$, $u$ takes every value in $\left[-\dfrac14,0\right)\cup\left(0,\dfrac34\right)$ ($u=-\dfrac14$ at integers $x$)
Graph of $\dfrac1u$: on $\left[-\dfrac14,0\right)$, $\dfrac1u$ takes all values in $(-\infty,-4]$ (including $-4$); on $\left(0,\dfrac34\right)$, all values in $\left(\dfrac43,\infty\right)$
Greatest integer: $(-\infty,-4]$ gives every integer $\leq-4$; $\left(\dfrac43,\infty\right)$ gives $1$ (from $\left(\dfrac43,2\right)$) and every integer $\geq2$
solution_full: Put $u=\{x\}-\dfrac14$. Since $\{x\}$ takes every value in $[0,1)$ and $\{x\}=\dfrac14$ is excluded, $u$ takes every value in $\left[-\dfrac14,0\right)\cup\left(0,\dfrac34\right)$; the end value $u=-\dfrac14$ occurs at every integer $x$.

The reciprocal $\dfrac1u$ is decreasing on each of the two pieces. On $\left[-\dfrac14,0\right)$ it runs from $-4$ (attained at $u=-\dfrac14$) down to $-\infty$, so it takes exactly the values in $(-\infty,-4]$.
On $\left(0,\dfrac34\right)$, $\dfrac1u$ runs from $+\infty$ down to $\dfrac43$ (not attained), so it takes exactly the values in $\left(\dfrac43,\infty\right)$.
Applying the greatest integer function: values in $(-\infty,-4]$ give every integer $n\leq-4$ (for instance $n$ itself is attained, since every $n\leq-4$ lies in $(-\infty,-4]$).
Values in $\left(\dfrac43,\infty\right)$ give $1$ (from values in $\left(\dfrac43,2\right)$) and every integer $n\geq2$ (from $\dfrac1u=n$).
No value of $\dfrac1u$ lies in $(-4,\dfrac43]$, so $[\,\cdot\,]$ never equals $-3,-2,-1$ or $0$ (these would need $\dfrac1u\in[-3,1)$, which is inside the gap).
Hence the range of $g$ is $\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{-3,-2,-1,0\}$, $S=\{-3,-2,-1,0\}$, and the sum of its elements is $-6$.
originality_note: New: the reciprocal of a shifted sawtooth {x} - 1/4 is passed through the greatest integer function, and the question asks which integers are missed, so both end-point behaviours (the attained -4 at integer x and the unattained 4/3) decide the answer (way 2). Closest known: range of 1/{x} or [1/x] type functions. Different because: the shift splits {x} - 1/4 into a negative and a positive branch with an asymmetric gap in 1/u, and the missing integers come from that gap.
blueprint_concepts: Standard functions and their graphs (polynomial, rational, modulus, signum, GIF, fractional part, exponential, logarithmic)

concept_use.Graphs of [f(x)], {f(x)} and 1/f(x): The graph of 1/u on [-1/4,0) and (0,3/4) and then the greatest integer of it give the range Z minus {-3,-2,-1,0}.
concept_use.Standard functions and their graphs (pol: The fractional part function {x} takes every value in [0,1), so u = {x} - 1/4 runs over [-1/4,0) union (0,3/4), with -1/4 attained at integers.

stem_review: Read as a student: [t] and {t} are defined, E excludes exactly the zeros of the denominator, the range and S are well defined and S is finite; answer -6 recomputed by sampling two million points and by hand; the end points -4 (attained) and 4/3 (not attained) checked; matches the plan 'negative integer'. Changed: No change.
key_step: Range of 1/u on [-1/4,0) union (0,3/4) is (-inf,-4] union (4/3, inf); the floor then misses exactly -3,-2,-1,0.
justification: Two ideas linked: the range of the fractional part with an excluded value, and the reciprocal graph with careful end-point handling before the greatest integer; one slip at an end point (1 or -4) changes the answer and there are no options. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q11 (L3), where a range must be examined for which integers it contains.
